title: YOUR SHADOW
REMEMBERS?

script.beat: 1 HOOK (0-3 s): the promise, stated as fact
script.text: What if your shadow remembered every step you took?

script.beat: 2 SETUP: the hypothetical, labelled, with one concrete image
script.text: Imagine it. You cross a sunlit room and the shape on the floor keeps the walk, like a drawing that will not fade.

script.beat: 3 TURN: the consequence, then the number
script.text: Turn around and it replays you. Leave, and it waits by the door. Every step is a mark: three thousand a day, a million a year.

script.beat: 4 CATCH + LOOP: the real mechanism, then the opening image again
script.text: But a shadow is only the place where light cannot reach. So it remembers nothing. You are the one who keeps every step.

science.claim: A shadow is the absence of light, not a record of events.
science.working: A shadow is formed where an opaque object blocks the light; it has no memory or structure of its own.
science.source: Basic optics; the shadow-memory premise is explicitly hypothetical

science.claim: A person takes roughly three thousand steps a day, about a million a year.
science.working: 3,000 x 365 = 1,095,000; the script rounds to a million. The step count varies widely by person and day.
science.source: Common public-health estimate; re-check the source before publishing

science.claim: A shadow moves when the light or the object moves.
science.working: The shadow is a projection of the blocked light, so its position and shape change with either.
